title: Pines grow faster and are more drought resilient in the Southern Hemisphere.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the Figshare deposit 'Data_nonnative_pines' (CC BY 4.0, 2026-09-03; it lists the paper as its reference) through DataCite. It holds 11 files: 10 R scripts and one data file, metadata_291225.csv (336 KB, semicolon-separated, decimal commas). That CSV has 1,625 tree rows and 34 columns: species (15), native/plantation/invasion status, country, lat/lon, elevation, tree diameter, d13C (carbon isotope ratio; 531 non-missing), wood density (1,338), and soluble sugars/starch/NSC (non-structural carbohydrates; 950 non-missing). It has 153 unique coordinate pairs and 132 location-site pairs. The scripts read the tree-ring width files (*.rwl in a local 'Procesadas/' folder) and SPEI (a drought index) climate series, and neither is in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 192 sites, the growth rates up to four times faster, and the drought resistance/resilience results come from the abstract and press coverage. The full text is paywalled and not in Europe PMC, so I did not read the paper's data availability statement.

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare deposit downloads openly (CC BY 4.0), but it contains only tree metadata and R scripts. The ring-width files the scripts read are not deposited (checked in the file list and the script code).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's outcomes are growth (basal area increment) and drought resistance/resilience. They would have to be computed from tree-ring width files and SPEI (a drought index) climate series, and neither is in the deposit (checked: the scripts read ./Procesadas/*.rwl). Only NSC (non-structural carbohydrates) and d13C (carbon isotope ratio) are present as measured columns.

a3_inputs_present.note: Per tree, the inputs are only species, status (native/plantation/invasion), coordinates, elevation and diameter. There are no ring-width series or climate data (checked in files).

a4_units_stated.note: The CSV has no units row or data dictionary. NSC is probably % dry mass and wood density g/cm³, but neither is stated in the deposit (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: The best available measured label is NSC, with 950 non-missing trees (d13C has 531) spread over about 153 site coordinates. That is under the ~1,500-row bar, and the real unit of independence is the site (checked in files).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The abstract says 192 sites. The CSV has 153 unique coordinate pairs and 132 location-site pairs, and I could not reconcile the two without the full text.

a8_label_provenance.note: NSC, d13C and wood density are lab measurements on tree samples, not model outputs.

backbone.name: none: tabular ecological data, no matching pretrained backbone

integration.partner_dataset: ITRDB (International Tree-Ring Data Bank) or TerraClimate/SPEI climate grids
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether non-native plantation growth advantages can be predicted from climate across sites. This cannot be tested without the undeposited ring-width series.

honest_claim_h3: With only the deposited table, a model could at best predict a tree's carbohydrate or carbon-isotope level from its species, status and site among about 950 sampled trees. That is a mixed-model statistics question, not an ML one.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a tree's species, location and native-versus-planted status to predict its growth rate and recovery after drought.
plain_idea.train_on: Tree-level records of species, site coordinates, elevation, trunk diameter and native/plantation/invasion status: 1,625 trees in the deposited table. The ring-width series needed for growth are not deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Growth and drought resilience, which come from tree-ring widths that are not public. The only measured labels in the deposit are sugar/starch reserves (950 trees) and carbon isotope ratio (531 trees), both lab assays on wood samples.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Foresters and carbon-offset planners in Chile, Argentina, New Zealand and South Africa would like to know where planted pines stay resilient. The deposit doesn't support that model, though.

ml_idea: Predict tree growth and drought resilience from species, site climate and native/non-native status. This is blocked: the ring-width files that define the label are not deposited.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 336 KB CSV; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the Figshare files and see whether any .rwl ring-width files are there. They are not (done).

verdict_reason: A2/A3: the growth and resilience outcomes need tree-ring width files and SPEI drought-index climate series, and the Figshare deposit leaves both out (verified from the file list and the R scripts). A5: the only measured labels deposited are NSC (non-structural carbohydrates, 950 trees) and d13C (carbon isotope ratio, 531 trees) across about 153 sites, with no units stated. That is too small and too thin on features for ML.
